title: Dimension X
paragraphs: NBC science-fiction anthology adapting stories by leading genre writers alongside original radio scripts, with tales of space travel, alien contact, future societies, and dangerous technology.

Adult NBC science-fiction anthology adapting major published SF alongside original radio plays. All 50 historical programs survive, but the frozen GRH snapshot represented in this Phase 3 run contains only programs 26-50. The first 25 are retained as documented archive-scope absence, not fabricated episode rows.

GRH documents the program through Complete 50-program NBC run (April 8, 1950 to September 29, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Frozen programs 26-34 (September 29, 1950 to January 14, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Frozen programs 35-50 (June 3, 1951 to September 29, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|norman-rose|Norman Rose]] (host on 25 recordings), William Welch (producer on 20 recordings), Albert Buhrman (music on 18 recordings), Edward King (director on 13 recordings), Ernest Kinoy (radio adaptor on 9 recordings and writer on 3 recordings), Fred Weihe (director on 12 recordings and transcriber on 8 recordings), and George Lefferts (radio adaptor on 11 recordings and writer on 1 recording).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.66865a83f6609315|KFI]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include adapted science-fiction literature, space exploration and interplanetary travel, technology, automation and scientific risk, alien contact and extraterrestrial life, human identity, androids and artificial persons, and nuclear war and post-apocalyptic society.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Adult science fiction becomes a sustained radio anthology, Published science-fiction adaptation pipeline, Five-month 1951 hiatus, and Dimension X scripts reused by X Minus One.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (70 shared credited people), [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (44 shared credited people), [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (33 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (31 shared credited people), and [[show|the-mysterious-traveler|The Mysterious Traveler]] (26 shared credited people).
